images.title: Nature's golden mirror
images.caption: A grove of pond cypress trees with fall foliage, Georgia, USA
images.desc: Reflected in calm water and glowing in the light of the setting sun, this grove of pond cypress creates a striking display of colour and symmetry. Native to the southeastern United States, the species is associated with shallow ponds, depressions and wetland habitats. This image was captured in Georgia, where these trees can be found in places such as the Okefenokee Swamp and other low-lying wetlands.

images.title: Nature's fall soundtrack
images.caption: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
images.desc: In Bulgaria's Western Rhodope Mountains, autumn leaves gather beside the rushing waters of Sitovo Waterfall. Near the village of Sitovo, southwest of Plovdiv, the falls tumble beneath an old stone bridge whose arch frames the cascades like a storybook scene. Moss-covered stones and pine trees add shades of green to the autumn landscape, while fallen leaves gather along the water's edge or drift through its pools. The falls become especially lively after rain and during spring snowmelt, when the surrounding woodland echoes with the sound of rushing water.

images.copyright: Mount Sneffels in the San Juan Mountains near Ridgway, Colorado, United States (© lightphoto/Getty Images)
images.title: 'Peak' into Colorado
images.caption: Mount Sneffels in the San Juan Mountains near Ridgway, Colorado
images.desc: Some mountains make you work for the view. Mount Sneffels makes you work for the last few hundred metres. Rising to 4,310 metres in Colorado's San Juan Mountains, this fourteener is a familiar sight around Ridgway, Ouray and Telluride. It sits within the 67-square-kilometre Mount Sneffels Wilderness, a protected area designated in 1980. Hikers can reach the mountain from several approaches, including the Yankee Boy Basin and the Blue Lakes area.

images.copyright: Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (© Antonio Salaverry/Shutterstock)
images.title: Bookishly extravagant
images.caption: Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
images.desc: Today we're inside the Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the humble act of opening a book took on grand architectural ambitions. Founded in 1837 by 43 Portuguese immigrants, just 15 years after Brazil's independence, the institution eventually moved into the building seen here, completed half a century later in a lavish Neo-Manueline style. Shelves soar over 20 metres around a vast reading room, crowned by a monumental stained-glass skylight that makes daylight part of the design.

images.title: Still waters, vivid colours
images.caption: Fall in Naejangsan National Park, South Korea
images.desc: Few places in South Korea capture the magic of fall quite like Naejangsan National Park, where mountainsides glow in brilliant shades of scarlet, orange, yellow and gold. Located in the country's southwest, the park is particularly famous for its vivid maple colours, making it one of Korea's premier destinations for fall scenery. Its name, meaning 'many secrets in the mountains,' reflects the varied landscapes found throughout the region.

images.title: Winging it over the river
images.caption: Nguyen Hoang Bridge, Hue, Vietnam
images.desc: Bridging the gap between old and new, Nguyen Hoang Bridge gives Hue's skyline a fresh connection. Spanning the Perfume River in Vietnam, the modern steel-arch landmark opened to traffic on March 26, 2025. Its design, called 'The Crane Facing Thien Mu,' draws inspiration from a local legend and nearby Thien Mu Pagoda.
